title: From crypto rails to open infrastructure: Ethereum’s expanding role
description:
Since the beginning of this year, I've been researching whether Ethereum, as a programmable, permissionless, publicly verifiable ledger, can serve industries beyond blockchain and crypto as a piece of critical infrastructure: as a payment layer (for open source funding), as a proof layer (for professionalised maintenance attestation), and as a coordination layer (for open-weight AI).

I will share findings and problems I've identified along the way, and would like to invite the audience to join a discussion: 
- From a tooling perspective, what kinds of tools or layers can we use or create (if they have not been built yet) to help us successfully apply Ethereum in other industries? 
- Where else might this pattern apply? Hypothetically, what other industries could benefit from using Ethereum as an infrastructural layer?
abstract: This talk presents findings from research in progress on Ethereum's payment / proof / coordination three-layer structure as critical infrastructure beyond blockchain / crypto. The idea is to expand your knowledge of how Ethereum can be used for cross-industry adoption and to give you food for thought on how you can help us achieve that adoption by building tools, layers and new infrastructure on top of the protocol.
